text.title: Response reference
text.description: Unique reference: LC02-OP-RESP- for ownership; LC-CONSULT-RESP- for consultation. Maximum 80 characters. Reuse only for an identical retry. Required for either response action.

text_1.title: Response / outcome
text_1.description: Ownership: Accepted or Declined. Consultation: Responded, Unanswered, Declined or Conditional. Responded does not mean policy approval. Required for either response action.

text_2.title: Reason / finding
text_2.description: Describe the response or outstanding work factually. Maximum 255 characters; retain unresolved conditions. Required for either response action.

text_3.title: Evidence reference
text_3.description: Retained evidence supporting this response. Maximum 255 characters; do not invent missing evidence. Required for either response action.

text_4.title: Next action
text_4.description: Describe the remaining step, including unresolved conditions. Maximum 2000 characters. No assignment or notification follows. Required for either response action.

text_5.title: Action
text_5.description: Choose the action for this selected case. Consultation stays closed until a prepared draft is verified. Enter exactly: Ownership response / Consultation response.

text_6.title: Case reference
text_6.description: Existing LC-FICTIONAL-OP- case reference. A lookup key only; no authority, role or document version is supplied by this field.

inputs.content:
FICTIONAL policy lifecycle qualification only.
This source establishes no clinical advice or policy authority.
Ownership: explicit proposal and acceptance are required in the simulation.

FICTIONAL PROCEDURE — EVIDENCE INDEX MAINTENANCE
Document identity: FICTIONAL-DOC-PPG-INDEX-20261018-02
Technical workflow test only. Not an operative policy, clinical instruction or staff assignment.

1. Locate the retained evidence reference and identify its source version.
2. Compare the proposed index description with the retained reference; record unresolved differences.
3. Keep a preserved historical reference when a draft index description changes.
4. Record the fictional review evidence separately from any source facts.

Optional note: evidence location changes do not establish content approval or permission to issue.
